title: The Forest Repeats
text: We made it to Whispering Kelp Forest! The currents really do whisper here. I said 'hello' and somewhere deeper in the trees something whispered 'hello' back. Then another voice said it. Then another. Glimmer has decided this is delightful. I have decided to choose my words very carefully~

title: Lanternvine Courtesy
text: The little Fae lights here disappear whenever I walk toward them. I finally stopped chasing one and politely pretended I couldn't see it. Five minutes later there were twelve following us. Apparently the secret to making friends in this forest is ignoring everyone.

title: Ask the Roots Nicely
text: Found three vines braided together across the path. An old carving says that's how travelers marked safe routes without hurting the forest. I asked the vines which way to go. One moved. I followed it. Glimmer followed a different one. We somehow ended up at the same place. I refuse to let the forest know this confused me.

title: A Forest Full of Stars
text: Silver pollen filled the water tonight, and every flower opened into the shape of a constellation. For a little while it looked like the entire sky had fallen into the forest. I recognized three constellations! Glimmer insists there were four. Glimmer is counting itself.

title: Please Stop Teaching the Vines
text: I showed one little vine how to open the buckle on my berry pouch. It showed another vine. That vine showed THREE MORE. I am currently being followed by a small gang of extremely talented thieves. I accept some responsibility and none of the blame.

title: They Came This Way Too
text: Found an old metal tag beneath the moss. It belonged to a search team sent to recover escaped experimental subjects. So the organization reached this forest too. The tag was completely wrapped in roots when I found it. Somehow that makes me feel a little better.

title: The Listening Grove
text: I heard my name today. Not from Glimmer. Not from another traveler. The forest whispered 'Shizuki' from somewhere behind me... then somewhere ahead... then from every direction at once. I did the sensible thing and whispered 'yes?' back. The forest laughed. I think.

title: Do Not Touch the Old Dreamsap
text: Fresh dreamsap apparently helps wounds heal. Old dreamsap stores the last nightmare of whatever touched it. Guess which kind I poked first. I am not writing down what I saw. I AM writing down that Glimmer spent the next hour sitting on my head, so I think that counts as emotional support.

title: Shrine Beneath the Roots
text: Found a tiny Fae shrine buried beneath the oldest roots. The strange part is that the forest grew completely around it without a single root crossing its shadow. I left a few berries there. Glimmer left something shiny. Neither of us knows the proper offering etiquette, but effort should count.

title: An Excellent Hiding Place
text: Found an old search map showing this grove was checked SIX TIMES. Six! Apparently they never found what they were looking for. Personally, I would have hidden inside the map cabinet. Nobody ever checks the map cabinet. ...Actually, I'm writing that down for later.

title: Moonmoth Migration
text: Hundreds of Moonmoths flew through the canopy tonight. There isn't enough visible sky down here for them to navigate by stars, but somehow they know exactly where they're going. I followed them for a while. Glimmer joined their formation and was accepted immediately. Traitor.

title: The Briar Treaty
text: Found an ancient tablet listing things you're forbidden from doing to this grove: no axes, no fire, no stealing living blooms, and—very specifically—no rude singing. I would like to know what happened for THAT rule to become necessary. I would also like everyone to know I did not test it.

title: A Voice From Long Ago
text: One of the vines keeps repeating the same command. I found the name attached to it in an old record... and whoever spoke those words has been gone for almost eighty years. The forest remembered their voice anyway. I'm starting to wonder how much this place remembers.

title: The Polite Apothecary
text: Apparently the old healers here only collected leaves that plants willingly dropped after being thanked. I tried it. 'Excuse me, may I have a leaf?' Nothing. 'Please?' Nothing. Glimmer chimed at the plant and THREE leaves fell. I have been professionally outperformed by a glowing ball.

title: Definitely a Normal Bush
text: I found the PERFECT hiding bush today. Huge leaves. Hollow center. Completely impossible to see through. I made a little sign that says: 'No escaped elf behind this shrub. Please direct search teams elsewhere. —Not Shizuki.' Glimmer thinks this makes the hiding place less effective. Glimmer lacks vision.

title: Too Many Shizukis
text: Found another pursuit record. They tracked an unusual Fae signature from Moonlit Reef all the way here... then the forest started producing hundreds of identical magical echoes. The search team couldn't tell which trail was real. I don't know if the forest was protecting me specifically, but I whispered 'thank you' anyway. Something whispered 'you're welcome.'

title: The Root Remembers
text: A huge root grew around an old metal restraint until the metal cracked into pieces. I stared at it longer than I meant to. The forest took something designed to hold someone captive and simply... kept growing until it broke. I think I like this place.

title: Whispercap Consensus
text: The whispercaps warn travelers about danger by repeating messages to each other until the whole colony agrees. Unfortunately, this takes HOURS. I heard: 'Danger... ahead... probably... maybe... yes... definitely.' By then Glimmer and I had already gone there and come back. Excellent system.

title: Ask Before Picking
text: Apparently you're allowed to collect fallen pods here, but stealing a living flower makes the forest take away your sense of direction. I was going to joke that I wouldn't notice the difference, but Glimmer chimed before I could finish. I KNOW WHAT THAT MEANS.

title: Searchlight Spores
text: Their detection spores make you glow bright green. Terrible for hiding. Fortunately, rolling in blue pollen makes you glow bright blue instead. Completely different color. Problem solved. Glimmer says this does not count as stealth. Glimmer has become extremely judgmental lately.

title: The Shrine in the Reflection
text: There's a shrine here that only appears in reflections. Look directly at the clearing? Nothing. Look at it through still water? Shrine. I tried measuring where it should be and it disappeared from the reflection too. Apparently even ancient Fae magic hates paperwork.

title: Letters to the Forest
text: I found an old figure made entirely from roots. Inside were hundreds of tiny folded letters from travelers asking the forest for guidance. Some wanted safe passage. Some wanted people they loved to come home. One just asked where they left their shoe. I hope the forest answered that one.

title: They Couldn't Find Me
text: Another pursuit report. Their captain wrote that the target's Fae signature couldn't be separated from the forest's own magic. The more I read, the stranger that feels. Were they following traces I left behind? Was the forest copying them? Either way... they never caught up.

title: The Forest Did Not Move
text: I marked our campsite with three stones last night. This morning the stones were twenty paces away. The trees insist—very loudly—that THEY did not move. I asked who did. Every whisper in the forest went silent. Suspicious.

title: Returned Access Card
text: Found an old facility access card tangled in the roots. The authorization stripe still works, which feels rude considering everything else here has been reclaimed by the forest. I painted little flowers over it. There. Much better security clearance.

title: Glimmerpod Nursery
text: Found a whole grove of Glimmerpods today! They slowly opened while I sat nearby, but snapped shut the moment I brought an old facility weapon close. I put the weapon down and they opened again. Glimmer is now sitting among them pretending to be one. Honestly? Convincing.

title: They Never Stopped Looking
text: The records keep going. Different names. Different Officers. Different handwriting. Same orders: find the escaped subjects. Whoever started the search was gone, and then someone else inherited it. Then someone else. It's strange seeing people continue a hunt when they probably don't even remember why it began.

title: The Forest Fought Back
text: I finally figured out why so many old search constructs are scattered around in circles. The roots learned to copy their tracking signals. Every time a construct thought it found its target, the forest sent the same signal somewhere else. Again. And again. And again. I LOVE THIS FOREST.

title: Still Missing
text: Found one of the last surviving pursuit ledgers today. Every page says the same thing beside Subject Seven: OUTSTANDING. No recovery date. No return record. Nothing saying they ever got me back. I already knew that, obviously. I'm standing here. Still... seeing it written down felt good.

title: The Forest Keeps Secrets
text:
At the deepest part of the forest, the roots have grown around an old archive. There are names inside connected to escapes, missing researchers, hidden routes... maybe even the rebellion. But whenever I try to read farther, the roots close over the pages. I could force them open. I won't. This forest kept my trail hidden long after everyone searching should have found it. If it wants to keep someone else's secrets too, that's fair.

Before we left, the currents whispered something new—one word I hadn't taught them: 'Leviathan.' Then the roots opened toward a path where every current bends in the same direction.

Glimmer went first.

Of course Glimmer went first.

Leviathan's Wake it is~
